title: nail drops a PTHR45685 hit when its forward and backward clouds do not meet in 5 attempts
body:
nail reports no hit for the PANTHER profile PTHR45685 (3,230 positions) against one spliced protein, `PTHR45685_NC_003281.10_spliced` (2,014 residues). hmmsearch and mmseqs both find it. A coworker of Jack's reported it. Copies of both files are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-17-lost-hit/input2` on the 16-core box.

hmmsearch 3.4 finds the target at 1,049.1 bits over three domains:

| domain | score | hmm | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 135.4 | 101-345 | 4-229 |
| 2 | 589.1 | 581-920 | 411-750 |
| 3 | 335.3 | 2026-2274 | 1770-2010 |

The target holds 13 runs of X, the longest at 859-1016 and 1349-1428, all between domains 2 and 3.

## What happens

The mmseqs seed spans all three domains: hmm 99-2273, target 2-2009, 793 bits, E 1.362e-240. The same seed and no hit come out of the `nail-v0.7.1` release binary, a build of `0a36fc0`, a build of `94eecda` (before nail-c34295), and `bb3c392`, at `-t 4` with mmseqs `8cc5ce3`.

`DefaultCloudSearchStage::run` in `nail/src/pipeline/cloud_stage.rs` runs a forward and a backward cloud search from the seed. If the two clouds are `Disjoint`, it scales α, β and γ by `1.0 + attempt * f` and tries again. After `-a` attempts (default 5, `-f` default 0.5), it returns `StageResult::Filtered`, and the seed is dropped before any score is computed. Here the clouds stay disjoint through 11 attempts and meet on the 12th:

| run, from the same seed | rows |
|---|---|
| defaults | 0 |
| `-C 2 -F 2 -E 1e300 -S 2`, every threshold off | 0 |
| `-a 10` or `-a 11` | 0 |
| `-a 12`, `-a 15` or `-a 20`, with or without thresholds | 1: 742.4 bits, E 5.6e-227, target 5-2009, hmm 102-2273 |
| `-a 20 -A 1000 -B 1000 -G 100` | 1: 745.5 bits, E 6.6e-228 |

The X runs are not the cause on their own. With every X deleted (1,627 residues), the seed is E 2.4e-202 and nail still reports nothing. With every X replaced by A, nail finds the hit at the defaults: 644.9 bits, E 1.3e-197. So the scores through the 1,000 residues between domains 2 and 3 decide whether the clouds meet. hmmsearch aligns nothing there.

nail scores 742 bits where hmmsearch scores 1,049, as expected: nail configures one hit per target, so one alignment crosses both gaps between the domains.

## Open

- Whether a seed whose clouds never meet should fall back to the seed's rectangle, as `trim_wings` failing already does a few lines further down, instead of being dropped.
- How often clouds fail to meet on true hits. A count of `Disjoint` filters on a large run, compared against hmmsearch, would say whether this is rare.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text: The official `nail-v0.7.1` release binary, `nail-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` from GitHub, published 2026-08-01, also reports the hit on the pair alone: 853.4 bits, E 1.7e-260, from the same seed (hmm 95-1972, target 5-1443, E 1.651e-311). Its row is identical to the build of `0a36fc0` made on the 16-core box, and it reports the hit at `-t 1`, `-t 4` and `-t 16`. A dev build also prints `nail 0.7.1` from `--version`, since `nail/Cargo.toml` is still 0.7.1 on `dev`, so the version string does not pin the commit the coworker ran.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text: The coworker ran mmseqs `18-8cc5c`, the same version as on the 16-core box, so the mmseqs version does not explain the different seed. Her seed E-value (1.362e-240) and ours (1.651e-311) differ by about 10^71, about 236 bits. Our seed scored 965 bits over all three domains, so hers fits an mmseqs alignment ending after domain 2, as she described. Ours sits below the smallest normal double, so the 236 bits is approximate. Still needed from her: the full nail command line, the seed line for this pair from `--seeds-out`, and the other queries and targets in the run, if any.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text: The PTHR45628 files studied first were the wrong pair; the coworker sent them by mistake. Every build found that hit. The earlier notes about it, and the release binary at `tmp-claude/2026-10-17-lost-hit/release-0.7.1`, describe that pair, not this one. The coworker ran mmseqs `18-8cc5c`, the same version as on the 16-core box.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text: The mmseqs alignment behind the seed, decoded from the CIGAR in the align db nail kept (`tmp-claude/2026-10-17-lost-hit/t2-bb3c392/align-db/adb`), is one nearly gapless alignment: 1,985 matched columns, 190 profile positions skipped and 23 target residues inserted, with no gap longer than 25 profile positions. All 1,000 target residues between hmmsearch domains 2 and 3 (751-1769) are aligned as matches, X runs included. hmmsearch leaves that stretch unaligned and joins the domains through its J state. Jack: nail's model cannot fix this, so a fallback rectangle and a higher default `-a` are both off the table.
